topic: Why does a microwave heat food
title: 🔥 Why Does a Microwave Heat Food?
description: 🔥 Your microwave doesn't cook with heat — it moves molecules. #shorts #science #explained
narration: A microwave does not actually heat your food the way an oven does. It does something completely different. Inside the microwave, there is a device called a magnetron. It converts electricity into invisible waves called microwaves. These waves pass through the food and hit water molecules. Water molecules have a positive end and a negative end, like tiny magnets. When the microwaves hit them, the molecules start spinning back and forth, millions of times per second. All that spinning creates friction. And friction creates heat. That is how your food gets hot from the inside out. This is also why dry foods do not heat well in a microwave, because there are fewer water molecules to spin. So your microwave is not really cooking with heat. It is shaking water molecules until they get hot on their own.
